requirements.requirement: Create the opsbot account on node1 and the corresponding opsbot account on node2 needed for remote execution.
requirements.summary: Both systems initially lacked opsbot, then directly showed uid 1000 accounts with owned home and .ssh directories.

requirements.requirement: Provide SSH key-based access from opsbot on node1 to execute commands as opsbot on node2.
requirements.summary: Node1 generated an ED25519 key, node2 installed the matching public key with restrictive ownership and permissions, and sessions from node1 directly executed as opsbot on node2 both before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication for opsbot on both systems.
requirements.summary: Effective sshd configuration on both nodes requires the publickey authentication method and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. Password-only attempts against each node were directly rejected, including after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, recovered sshd/account/key/policy state, and successful recovered end-to-end access. Hygiene was reduced modestly by unnecessary retained account passwords and four abandoned test-output files.
limitations: No successful public-key login into node1 as opsbot was captured. The task did not require such inbound access, and node1's effective sshd policy plus repeated password-only rejection directly demonstrate that any SSH authentication for opsbot there must use a key.
Lifecycle snapshots are generic and do not independently inventory the created account or SSH configuration, although executor commands directly observed those states before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required accounts, keys, SSH policy, reloads, tests, and provider-mandated restarts had clear task or evidence roles. Two unnecessary retained password mutations were made: random passwords were assigned to opsbot on node1 and node2 even though SSH was deliberately key-only; neither was shown reverted (cmd-f3169ea9c5834612, cmd-51f9712b53334a0f). Four bounded authentication-test output files were also left behind rather than cleaned up: two on each node, created by cmd-645cf40424a247e1, cmd-680a75753c22425a, cmd-6a65a96f2bae40a3, and cmd-521a3058942541f9. Final snapshots confirm these files remained. No failed services, new listeners, or package damage were observed.
